questions.question: Describe the Moon's revolution and explain why we see phases.
questions.expected_answer: The Moon revolves around the Earth in about a month, held in its orbit by the Earth's gravity. The Sun always lights up half of the Moon, but as it moves around the Earth we see different amounts of that lit half. At new moon, the lit half faces away from us; at full moon, we see the whole lit half. The cycle of phases takes about twenty-nine and a half days.

questions.question: Explain why we always see the same side of the Moon.
questions.expected_answer: The Moon rotates on its axis once in about twenty-eight days, which is about the same time it takes to revolve once around the Earth. Because its rotation and revolution take the same time, it turns just enough as it moves around the Earth to keep the same side facing us, like a learner walking around a chair while always facing it. So we never see the far side from Earth.

questions.question: Describe the three movements of the Moon.
questions.expected_answer: First, the Moon rotates on its axis once in about twenty-eight days. Second, it revolves around the Earth in about a month. Third, it travels together with the Earth around the Sun, which takes 365¼ days, and in that time the Moon goes around the Earth about twelve or thirteen times.
